Our lab trains and evaluates large language models (LLMs) across both defensive and offensive security. On the defensive side, it includes triage, mitigation, remediation, detection engineering, and digital forensics. On the offensive side, this includes penetration testing, red teaming, vulnerability discovery, and exploitation. We host our task experts on inference platforms, models specialized for individual security tasks, for use by other companies as well as internally. As an Applied AI Scientist/Engineer, you will help shape Averlon's research agenda and model capabilities. You will train, evaluate, and benchmark LLMs on real-world security tasks, design reinforcement learning environments, and help publish findings that advance the field. Research at Averlon spans LLM post-training involving continual learning, reinforcement learning, as well as agentic tool use, evaluation design, and large-scale benchmarking. You will work closely with our research team and alongside engineers with deep security expertise, who will help you learn the cybersecurity domain on the job. Key Responsibilities Benchmark open-weight and proprietary LLMs on hundreds of offensive and defensive security tasks. RL of LLMs for security use cases as a post-training or continual learning process. This involves designing RL environments and reward signals for security tasks, including agentic settings that involve multi-step tool use. Track the research literature, reproduce relevant results, and assess new methods for adoption. Document results, negative as well as positive, to support internal decision-making. Contribute to research papers, technical reports, and blog posts that communicate the lab's findings to the wider community. Required Skills and Qualifications Strong grounding in deep learning, evidenced by coursework and hands-on projects in which you trained DNNs or fine tuned LLMs/VLMs. Working knowledge of transformer architectures, attention mechanisms, and language (or vision) models training. Proficiency in Python and in PyTorch or a comparable deep learning framework. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to design rigorous experiments and draw sound conclusions from them. Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical results to researchers and engineers. Prior knowledge of cybersecurity or compute clouds is not necessary. You will learn the domain on the job, working alongside our team. Preferred Qualifications Hands-on experience with LLM post-training or continual learning. Experience applying reinforcement learning, particularly to language models. Publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, or EMNLP, including workshop papers and preprints. Open-source contributions or software projects that others have adopted. Experience running and debugging distributed training on multi-node GPU systems. Education and Experience An MS or PhD from the IITs, ISI, IISER, IISc, BITS Pilani, the IIITs, or top NITs is preferred. MS and PhD graduates do not need prior professional experience. You’ll be responsible for defining system architecture, developing robust and secure applications, and mentoring junior engineers. This role demands a deep technical understanding, strong problem-solving abilities, and a passion for building impactful software that drives the healthcare industry forward. Troubleshoots and debugs non-routine issues spanning application layers and common OCI services; proposes fixes. Translates ambiguous requirements into scalable designs and implementation plans. Defines and stabilizes API contracts and dependencies for the application area. Systematically incorporates external feedback (forums, live-site reports) into backlog refinement. Mentors junior engineers; coordinates cross-functionally on feature delivery. Utilizes working knowledge to develop new software features and enhancements following design specifications and develops documents to clarify software design and code. Exercises judgment and discretion to conduct performance profiling and optimization of coding. Troubleshoots and resolves moderately complex issues related to application programming interface (API) functionality and integration. Implements moderately complex API versioning, lifecycle, and interoperability strategies. Software Architecture - Software System Structural Design: Designs and develops software, systems, and services aligned to pre-defined system architecture. Develops working knowledge of software architecture decisions and best practices. Collaborates with team leads to review work to ensure alignment with software architecture. Implements moderately complex performance optimization and scalability strategies in software design. May provide technical guidance and support to customers regarding customer-reported issues, independently. Coaches, mentors, and guides others to advocate for customers' interests and suggests product enhancements based on feedback. Influences team to ensure customer satisfaction through timely resolution of issues and effective communication. Implements customer issue and/or defect handling and training processes, independently. Investigates and troubleshoots complex product maintenance issues to ensure customer agreement on short- and long-term solutions (e.g., future enhancements). Practices and Standards Compliance - Security and Compliance: Collaborates with the team to establish and follow development practices and coding standards. Exercises judgment and discretion to ensure code quality and adherence to broad acceptance criteria during development. Keeps up-to-date with industry best practices and applies them to software development processes. Implements secure coding practices to prevent security vulnerabilities. Development Operations - System Maintenance: Performs periodic maintenance and testing operations for systems that require upgrading or patching (e.g., for critical vulnerabilities). Exercises judgment and discretion to drive improvements, ensure automation, testing, and debugging of systems to ensure service/product availability, health, support, and reliability. Core Responsibilities Planning & Execution: Independently manages work, monitoring timelines and deliverables to ensure projects or initiatives stay on track and meet requirements. Proactively prioritizes work and adapts to resource or timeline shifts, suggesting adjustments to maintain project efficiency. Collaboration & Partnership: Collaborates across teams to align on expectations and achieve shared objectives. Builds and maintains a comprehensive understanding of business, stakeholder, and/or customer needs to build and support effective partnerships. Actively listens to diverse perspectives and asks questions to ensure understanding of others. Problem Solving: Independently identifies and addresses standard and non-standard issues in accordance with standard practices, escalating more complex issues as appropriate. Analyzes data and/or information from multiple sources to troubleshoot standard and non-standard errors. Contributes to knowledge sharing and best practices. Continuous Learning: Embraces continuous learning by actively seeking to build knowledge and new skills and/or tools and staying current with industry trends and best practices. Seeks out and leverages feedback and training to improve skills. Contributes to a culture of continuous learning and knowledge sharing with team members. Continuous Improvement: Develops ideas and recommends updates to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of processes, protocols, and workflows within a team. Seeks input from team members on alternative approaches and methods for improving work. The engineer establishes clear operational ownership, improves monitoring and recovery readiness, standardizes repeatable engineering practices, and resolves complex service issues. By expanding senior-level engineering coverage and reducing dependency on a limited number of key resources, the role enables architects and senior leaders to spend more time on architecture, governance, security, and strategic priorities rather than routine operational work. Key Responsibilities Design, implement, and maintain critical infrastructure, security platforms, and enterprise services across cloud and on-premises environments. Convert approved requirements and architecture standards into secure, reliable, and supportable production solutions. Take end-to-end technical ownership for assigned platforms and services, including configuration standards, documentation, monitoring, patching, upgrades, capacity planning, vendor coordination, incident support, lifecycle planning, and continuous improvement. Increase delivery capacity across infrastructure and security initiatives by leading or executing technical work packages, resolving dependencies, coordinating testing and change activities, and completing operational handover with service owners and support teams. Accelerate modernization and reduce technical debt by identifying aging, unsupported, overly complex, or manually administered technologies; developing practical remediation or replacement plans; and implementing standardized, automated, and maintainable solutions. Reduce lifecycle-management and remediation backlogs by assessing platform health, prioritizing work based on operational and security risk, coordinating maintenance windows, and completing upgrades, patching, configuration remediation, and technology refresh activities. Improve operational resilience by engineering platforms for availability, recoverability, scalability, and secure operation. Establish monitoring, alerting, backup, recovery, and failover requirements; validate procedures through testing; and address identified gaps. Automate repeatable infrastructure and operational tasks using scripting, configuration management, infrastructure as code, and orchestration tools. Maintain version-controlled code, technical standards, reusable modules, and tested deployment and rollback procedures. Troubleshoot complex incidents and recurring service issues using logs, metrics, traces, platform telemetry, and root-cause analysis. Implement corrective actions, document known errors and recovery procedures, and reduce repeated manual intervention. Engineer and operate services in alignment with approved security requirements. Apply least privilege, secure configuration, secrets and certificate management, vulnerability remediation, logging, segmentation, and access-control standards; identify and escalate exceptions or material risks. Improve team coverage and reduce key-person dependency by creating current architecture diagrams, build standards, inventories, operating procedures, support runbooks, and knowledge articles. Crosstrain colleagues and ensure critical services have effective primary and secondary support coverage. Partner with Architecture, Security, Service Management, application teams, and business stakeholders to evaluate technical options, explain tradeoffs, sequence work, and ensure solutions meet operational, security, compliance, and business requirements.
